question: For the five pinned raw-C Gamma_1,p=0 zero-shell roots, do two finite plus-end Weyl initializations and two finite minus-end characteristic evaluations numerically agree with the previously conditional moving-boundary F_lambda identity near lambda=0?

upstream_results.role: pins exactly five declared sign-changing Gamma_1,p=0 zero-shell root centers and the p=plus/minus sqrt(2/3) kappa convention
pins the conditional Mellin/Lagrange prediction F_lambda(0)=-N_f/(2 a), its five a and N_f values, and its explicitly local scope

primary_sources.source: E. A. Coddington and N. Levinson, Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations (1955), chapters 1 and 3
primary_sources.used_for: linear-system fundamental-solution existence and Wronskian/Lagrange bookkeeping on finite intervals
primary_sources.not_used_for: turning a finite-cutoff numerical Weyl initialization into an exact endpoint theorem

primary_sources.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, sections 10.25, 10.29 and 10.40
primary_sources.used_for: the lambda=0 K_(i kappa) convention and large-positive-z derivative convention used only to calibrate the finite plus-end initialization
primary_sources.not_used_for: a nonzero-lambda spectral measure, rigging map, or constraint-rescaling equivalence

primary_sources.source: I. S. Gradshteyn and I. M. Ryzhik, Table of Integrals, Series, and Products, 8th ed., formula 6.576(4)
primary_sources.used_for: the already-pinned weighted K-square Mellin norm in the conditional F_lambda reference value
primary_sources.not_used_for: proving an absolute spectral normalization or physical inner product

declared_conventions.reference_boundary_pair: c(Q_0)=1,c'(Q_0)=0, solved at lambda=0 for the pinned p
declared_conventions.finite_minus_characteristic: F_Qminus(lambda;p)=-W(u_lambda,c)(Q_minus), where u_lambda is normalized by u_lambda(Q_0)=1 after backwards propagation
declared_conventions.lambda_zero_reference: u_0(Q)=K_(i*kappa)(6*pi^2 exp(Q))/K_(i*kappa)(z_0), F_lambda(0)=-N_f/(2 a) before this normalization and equals -N_f/(2 a^2) after it
declared_conventions.plus_end_initialization: u(Q_plus)=1, u'(Q_plus)=-(sqrt(A)+A'/(4A)), A=(72*pi^4 exp(2Q)+12*pi^2 lambda exp(3Q/2)-3p^2)/2; finite-Q_plus WKB only
declared_conventions.numeric_dtype: numpy.float64 with upstream decimal strings rounded only at the finite-ODE comparison boundary

assumptions: the pinned five roots are local centers only; no root continuation or classification outside that finite census is attempted
the large-positive-Q WKB datum is an explicitly finite approximate proxy for the nonzero-lambda plus-end Weyl solution; agreement between two Q_plus values is a cutoff control, not an endpoint proof

all backward propagation uses a two-component linear system with segmentwise amplitude renormalization, never a Riccati/log-derivative evolution; nodes therefore do not cause a division-by-u pole in the main route
the nonzero value at Q_0 required to normalize u_lambda is checked separately for every root, lambda, and plus cutoff

the finite-Q_minus characteristic uses the Wronskian against the fixed lambda=0 reference pair; its stabilization is required because it is not valid to substitute u_lambda'(Q_0) for this quantity at lambda nonzero
the conditional-Jacobian upstream prediction is a comparison reference, not assumed to be numerically established by this new finite-cutoff test
tasks: verify both upstream result hashes, payload hashes, verdicts, and five-root agreement
derive the finite-interval linear ODE, Wronskian sign, and scale conversion of the conditional F_lambda prediction after u(Q_0)=1 normalization
for every root and every lambda delta, integrate a scaled two-component system backward from each Q_plus, normalize at Q_0, then integrate u_lambda and c to both Q_minus values and evaluate -W there

compare central finite differences on the fixed delta ladder with the pinned conditional prediction; check delta refinement, plus cutoff, minus cutoff, lambda-zero residual, normalization denominator, parity, and Wronskian consistency
fail closed if a node-induced normalization zero, solver failure, nonpositive plus-end A, missing finite-difference plateau, cutoff drift, or disagreement exceeds declared tolerances

decision_table.condition: all finite-difference, cutoff, normalization, parity and conditional-prediction controls pass
any upstream, solver, normalization, plateau, cutoff, or comparison control fails
